text.text:
Yann LeCun’s startup just came out of stealth and raised $1.03 billion in its first funding round, at a reported $3.5 billion pre-money valuation. For a company that is less than three months old and still pre-product, that is an extraordinary signal about how much capital is now chasing alternative AI architectures beyond mainstream LLM scaling. 

The company is Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI), and the pitch is very LeCun: reasoning, planning, and world models instead of pure next-token prediction. Reuters says the round was co-led by Cathay Innovation, Greycroft, Hiro Capital, HV Capital, and Bezos Expeditions. 

The Financial Times goes further and describes it as Europe’s largest ever seed round, which makes the scale even more remarkable. It also reports additional backing from Temasek, SBVA, and Nvidia, and names Alexandre LeBrun as CEO, with LeCun as executive chair. 

The deeper takeaway is not just that LeCun raised a lot of money. It is that investors are now willing to place billion-dollar bets on the idea that the next leap in AI may come from new architectures, not just bigger language models. That is a very important shift in the market narrative.
